intro.text: For Insurance Data Sharing, the Permissions field is an array of { InsuranceType, Permissions[] } objects — permissions are scoped to a specific insurance type, so a TPP can request different data clusters per type in a single consent.

headers: What the user sees on both the Consent and Authorisation pages

intro.text: Each entry in Permissions nominates an InsuranceType. The LFI Authorisation Page only shows policies whose type appears in the consent — this acts as the equivalent of Banking’s AccountSubType filter.

rows: Only policies whose InsuranceType matches one of the requested values are shown for selection. If the user holds no policies of any requested type, the LFI returns the no-matching-policies error and the authorisation flow cannot proceed.
Invalid — Permissions must contain at least one entry and each entry must declare an InsuranceType. The consent is rejected before authorisation begins.

intro.text: Only request the insurance types your service genuinely needs. Listing extra types forces the user to scan irrelevant policies and is flagged during CX certification.

Policies are grouped on the Authorisation Page by their Status field ( AEInsurancePolicyStatusCodes ). Currently active statuses are presented first and selectable by default; end-state statuses are bucketed into a collapsible Inactive Policies group so the user can see what is in scope but cannot select policies whose data can’t be shared.

rows: Shown first, with a green tick header. Selectable by default.
Expired, Lapsed, Cancelled, Surrendered, Converted, DeathClaim, RiderClaim
Collapsed by default behind an amber clock header. The policy’s end-state status is shown below the insurance type so the user understands why the policy is not selectable.

intro.text: When a TPP acts on behalf of another entity (e.g. an aggregator operating under a different trading name), OnBehalfOf.TradingName identifies the entity to the user on both the Consent and Authorisation pages.

rows: The trading name is displayed in the page copy so the user clearly understands which entity they are sharing data with.
The TPP’s registered name is displayed in place of the trading name.

intro.text: Always populate OnBehalfOf.TradingName so users see a recognisable name rather than a blank or placeholder.
